root_cause.text: do_swap_page() used a busy-wait (spinning) loop with folio_trylock() when attempting to acquire the lock of a device-private folio for migration, which could cause a livelock when the lock holder was waiting for a work item on the same CPU (e.g., via lru_add_drain_all()), preventing the work item from executing.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "If hmm_range_fault() fails a folio_trylock() in do_swap_page, trying to acquire the lock of a device-private folio for migration, to ram, the function will spin until it succeeds grabbing the lock." and "Resolve this by waiting for the folio to be unlocked if the folio_trylock() fails in do_swap_page()." The patch changes the failure path from `pte_unmap_unlock` (which would release locks but allow retry in a spin loop) to calling `softleaf_entry_wait_on_locked()` to properly sleep until the folio is unlocked.

Avoid multiple CPU page faults to the same device page racing by trying
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 1afaeb8293c9addbf4f9140bdd22635fed763459
Author: Matthew Brost <matthew.brost@intel.com>
Date:   Wed Mar 5 17:26:28 2025 -0800

    mm/migrate: Trylock device page in do_swap_page
    
    Avoid multiple CPU page faults to the same device page racing by trying
    to lock the page in do_swap_page before taking an extra reference to the
    page. This prevents scenarios where multiple CPU page faults each take
    an extra reference to a device page, which could abort migration in
    foli

The vulnerable busy-wait spinning loop (e.g., while (!trylock_page(...))) is not present. The commit replaces the prior get_page/put_page pattern with a non-spinning trylock, so the function does not contain the vulnerable construct and the fix is already in place.
